title: Base Camp check
summary: A short adaptive check across Java, Big-O, data structures and patterns that suggests where to start. It places you; it doesn't grade you.

questions.prompt: True or false: in Java, == compares the characters of two Strings.
What does map.getOrDefault(key, 0) do when key isn't in the map?
options: Adds key with the value 0 and returns 0

questions.prompt: What does this program print?
What does this program print?
Complete the loop header so it visits every character of s.
What does this program print?
Dog extends Animal and overrides speak(). After Animal a = new Dog(); which speak() does a.speak() run?
options: Dog's, chosen at run time from the object's actual class
Animal's, because a is declared as an Animal
It doesn't compile without a cast

options: A stack (for example ArrayDeque used with push/pop)
An ArrayList, adding and removing at the end

questions.prompt: New orders keep arriving, and the cheapest pending order must always be processed next. Which structure?
options: A list, sorted again after every new order
A HashMap from order id to order

questions.prompt: For each incoming username you must say whether it has been seen before. Which structure?
Find the longest contiguous part of an array whose sum is at most k (all numbers are positive). Which technique would you investigate first?
options: Sliding window: grow on the right, shrink from the left while the sum is too big
Binary search on the first element

questions.prompt: Find two numbers in an unsorted array that add up to a target. Which approach?
options: One pass with a hash map from each value to its index, looking up target − x
Sort, then move two pointers inward
Binary search for target − x without sorting
